churches.name: Cornerstone Chapel, an Apostolic Church
churches.denomination: Apostolic (Oneness Pentecostal — independent or United Pentecostal Church affiliation)

score_notes.christology: Oneness Apostolic theology rejects the Trinity — teaches Jesus-Only modalism (Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are not distinct persons but modes of one God = Jesus). This is a historic heresy (condemned at Nicaea/Constantinople).
score_notes.soteriology: Apostolic churches typically teach baptismal regeneration and speaking in tongues as necessary for salvation — 'Acts 2:38 salvation plan' that adds works to justification by faith alone.
score_notes.denomination: Apostolic/Oneness tradition stands outside Nicene orthodoxy; no accountability to historic trinitarian Christianity.

churches.assessment: Cornerstone Chapel is an Apostolic/Oneness Pentecostal church — and that's a hard stop for theological alignment. Oneness Pentecostalism denies the eternal distinction of the three persons of the Trinity (Father, Son, Holy Spirit), teaching instead that 'Jesus' is the only name of God and the three are merely different modes. This places it outside the bounds of Nicene orthodoxy — the same line historic Christianity drew in 325 AD. Additionally, most Apostolic churches teach that speaking in tongues and baptism in 'Jesus' name only' are necessary for salvation, adding works to justification. The congregation may be sincere and passionate, but the core theological framework disqualifies it for anyone committed to trinitarian Christianity and faith-alone soteriology. Not recommended.

churches.name: Hope Presbyterian Church
churches.pastor: Jonathan Dennis (Senior Pastor); Chrishon Ducker (Associate Pastor)
churches.pastor_credentials: Jonathan Dennis: BA Biblical Studies, Grove City College 2011; MDiv, Reformed Theological Seminary 2017; EPC ordained since 2010

score_notes.gender: EPC is more conservative than mainline Presbyterians but allows each congregation some latitude on women's ordination as a 'constitutional scruple.' RTS-trained pastors tend complementarian, but official EPC stance is softer than PCA. Needs direct confirmation at local level.
score_notes.mens: No dedicated men's ministry found on website.

churches.assessment: Hope Presbyterian is one of the strongest finds on this list. Pastor Jonathan Dennis holds an MDiv from Reformed Theological Seminary — one of the top conservative Reformed seminaries in the world — and has been in EPC ministry since 2010. The EPC is a conservative evangelical Presbyterian denomination that affirms inerrancy, salvation by faith alone, and Nicene orthodoxy. It sits to the right of mainline Presbyterians (PCUSA) but slightly more latitude than the PCA on women's ordination (letting local congregations set policy). With an RTS-trained lead pastor, the preaching quality and doctrinal grounding should be excellent. The church is mission-focused (Great Commission language throughout) and serves the broader FXBG/Spotsylvania/Stafford/King George area. A serious candidate for Moop's home church search.

churches.name: Fredericksburg United Methodist Church
churches.pastor: Rev. Regina L. Anderson-Cloud (Senior Pastor); Ohhwan Freedman Kim (Associate Pastor); Chelsea Ann Morse (Associate Pastor)
churches.pastor_credentials: Unknown credentials for current pastoral team
churches.denomination: United Methodist Church (Virginia Annual Conference, Mission River District)

score_notes.scripture: UMC's 2024 General Conference officially removed the 'incompatibility' language around homosexuality and opened the door to full LGBTQ+ inclusion in ordination and marriage. The denomination has formally abandoned biblical authority on sexual ethics.
score_notes.gender: Female senior pastor; UMC fully ordains women at all levels. Denomination formally affirms same-sex marriage as of 2024 GC.
score_notes.leadership: Female senior pastor; multi-pastor team with no male-elder framework; UMC episcopal hierarchy is progressive.
score_notes.cultural: Post-2024 UMC is explicitly LGBTQ+ affirming at the denominational level. Many conservative churches left to form Global Methodist Church — those who stayed are the progressive/moderate wing.
score_notes.denomination: Virginia Annual Conference UMC — progressive denominational accountability; the traditional/conservative wing largely departed by 2023-24.

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg UMC sits squarely in the post-split United Methodist Church — the branch that retained 'United Methodist' branding after the traditional/conservative wing departed to form the Global Methodist Church. The 2024 UMC General Conference removed all language restricting LGBTQ+ ordination and same-sex marriage. With a female senior pastor, multiple associate pastors, and UMC denominational accountability to a now-affirming hierarchy, this church does not align with Moop's theological convictions. The congregation may have sincere Christ-loving people in the pews, but the institutional framework is compromised.

churches.name: Calvary Chapel Fredericksburg
churches.denomination: Calvary Chapel Association (independent with CC affiliation)

score_notes.denomination: Calvary Chapel Association is a loose affiliation rather than a formal denomination; provides some accountability but less structured than SBC or PCA.
score_notes.mens: Joe Gallegos serves as dedicated Men's Ministry leader on staff — an explicit men's discipleship investment.

churches.assessment: Calvary Chapel Fredericksburg checks most of the boxes Moop cares about. The Calvary Chapel movement is known above all for verse-by-verse expository Bible teaching — it's baked into the DNA (Chuck Smith legacy). The leadership page shows a clear elder/pastor structure with male pastoral leadership, a dedicated Men's Ministry leader (Joe Gallegos), and a full complement of ministries including youth, children, prayer, and outreach. CC churches typically hold to Scripture inerrancy, salvation by grace through faith alone, and complementarian leadership. The charismatic-adjacent culture (CC is Spirit-friendly but not charismatic in the more extreme sense) may be a moderate fit for Moop's background. The verse-by-verse preaching model is one of the best in evangelical Christianity. Strong candidate.

churches.name: Trinity Episcopal Church
churches.pastor: The Rev. Suzanne Hood (Rector, She/Her); The Rev. Bambi Willis; The Rev. Ethan Lowery (Campus & Young Adult Missioner, He/Him)
churches.pastor_credentials: Rev. Hood: Episcopal ordained clergy; Diocese of Virginia
churches.services: Sunday 8:00 AM (Rite I), 9:15 AM (Rite II), 11:15 AM; (540) 373-2996
churches.overall_label: Not Recommended — Same Concerns as St. George's

score_notes.scripture: TEC has formally abandoned biblical authority on sexuality — full LGBTQ+ affirmation, same-sex marriage, LGBTQ+ ordination all official denomination positions.
score_notes.gender: Female rector with she/her pronouns explicitly listed on church website; TEC fully ordains women at all levels including bishop.
score_notes.leadership: Female rector, TEC's progressive hierarchy provides denominational 'accountability' to an affirming structure.
score_notes.cultural: Website: 'ALL are welcome. We are a vibrant and inclusive community of seekers.' Inclusive identity language is front and center; 'inclusive community of seekers' framing suggests broad pluralism rather than Great Commission clarity.
score_notes.mission: 'We serve God by loving and serving others' — service/community framing without clear Great Commission language.

churches.assessment: Trinity Episcopal has the same fundamental problem as St. George's Episcopal: it belongs to The Episcopal Church (TEC), which has made formal, binding institutional commitments to LGBTQ+ affirmation that place it outside biblical alignment. The rector lists she/her pronouns on the church website, men serve with he/him pronouns listed — pronoun-aware staff culture is a visible marker of TEC's progressive institutional identity. Founded in 1877, Trinity has a rich liturgical history and likely has sincere Christians in the congregation, but the denominational framework and leadership culture are incompatible with Moop's convictions. The 'inclusive community of seekers' branding further flags a therapeutic/inclusive ecclesiology rather than a word-and-sacrament Great Commission model. Not recommended.

churches.name: Chancellor Baptist Church
churches.overall_label: Visit with Discernment — BGAV Caution Applies

score_notes.gender: BGAV (Baptist General Association of Virginia) is the moderate/progressive Virginia Baptist body and allows women in pastoral roles. Local stance on gender unknown — must ask directly.
score_notes.leadership: Pastor Cameron West; no visible elder board structure confirmed. BGAV-affiliated so denominational accountability is to a moderate body.
score_notes.cultural: No explicit DEI language found on website; the mission is gospel-clear ('to reach those without a church home'; 'point others to God'). But BGAV affiliation carries latent risk.
score_notes.denomination: BGAV is the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship-adjacent body in Virginia — moderate theologically, left the SBC years ago over inerrancy and gender issues.
score_notes.preaching: Preaching style not confirmed from website. The beliefs statement is solid: inerrancy affirmed, salvation through Christ, immersion baptism, eternal security.
score_notes.mens: No dedicated men's ministry confirmed on website.

churches.assessment: Chancellor Baptist's doctrinal statement is genuinely solid — they affirm Scripture as God's Word, salvation through Christ alone, eternal security, baptism by immersion, Great Commission evangelism. The church's mission statement (pointing people to Christ and into His church) is clear and healthy. The honest concern is BGAV affiliation: unlike SBC, BGAV is the moderate Virginia Baptist stream that parted ways over inerrancy and women's ordination. That doesn't automatically mean Chancellor is progressive — many BGAV churches are theologically conservative at the local level — but the accountability structure is to a moderate denomination. Before joining, Moop should ask: Does Chancellor have an elder board? What is the stance on women in pastoral roles? Pastor Cameron West's background and convictions are unknown — worth a direct conversation.

churches.name: Antioch Community Church (Fredericksburg area)

score_notes.christology: No data found to score; defaulting yellow.

churches.assessment: Extensive web research failed to surface a specific 'Antioch Community Church' operating in Fredericksburg, Spotsylvania, or Stafford County VA with a confirmed web presence. Churches by this name found were in Lunenburg County, VA (rural, not FXBG area) and Scottsville, VA. It is possible this church has minimal online presence, operates under a slightly different name, or is a newer plant. Before visiting, try Google Maps search or direct community referral to confirm location and basic beliefs. All rubric items are scored yellow to reflect 'unknown' rather than alignment or misalignment.

churches.name: Grace Church of Fredericksburg
churches.pastor: Pastor Ernest (last name unconfirmed); Dick Blackwell (founder, 1979)
churches.founded: 1979 (Grace Network plant by Dick Blackwell of Harrisonburg)

score_notes.gender: Gender/complementarian stance unknown; no explicit statement found.
score_notes.leadership: Leadership structure not publicly detailed; 'elders and pastors' mentioned in one description but not enumerated on website.
score_notes.cultural: Mission language ('Encounter God, Experience Family, Extend Christ's Kingdom, Empowered by the Spirit') is theologically sound but heavy Spirit-emphasis may indicate charismatic culture. No DEI/CRT language found.
score_notes.denomination: Grace Network is a loose charismatic/evangelical church-planting network. Less structured than a denomination.
score_notes.preaching: Preaching style not confirmed; Spirit-emphasis may mean topical/experiential rather than expository.
score_notes.mens: No men's ministry confirmed on website.

churches.assessment: Grace Church of Fredericksburg has a 45-year track record — planted in 1979 by Grace Network, a charismatic/evangelical church-planting ministry. The mission statement is Christ-centered and kingdom-focused. The church has a meaningful Facebook/social presence with 2,200+ followers. Reviews describe a welcoming community where Pastor Ernest and leadership genuinely love God and their congregation. The Spirit-emphasis framing ('Empowered by the Spirit,' 'transforming presence and power') suggests a charismatic worship culture. Key unknowns: preaching style (expository vs. topical), stance on gender roles, leadership accountability structure. Worth a visit if you're comfortable with a Spirit-forward evangelical culture; go in with questions about elder structure and biblical authority.

churches.name: Living Water Christian Center Church (LWC3)
churches.pastor: Pastor John Butler (Lead Pastor); Pastor Melanie Butler (Co-Pastor)
churches.services: Sundays (check website); midweek Bible study available; (540) 373-6310

score_notes.gender: Pastor Melanie Butler serves as co-pastor alongside her husband — complementarian yellow flag. Husband-wife co-pastor team is common in charismatic independent churches but doesn't align with male-elder conviction.
score_notes.leadership: Husband-wife pastoral team with no visible elder board structure; accountability structure unknown for independent church.
score_notes.denomination: Fully independent; no external denominational accountability.
score_notes.preaching: Described as teaching 'the Word of God with clarity and understanding'; Pentecostal/charismatic context suggests some topical/experiential preaching likely.

churches.assessment: Living Water Christian Center Church (LWC3) leads with solid language: 'Offering Christ, Loving People, Empowering through the Word,' 'the infallible word of Jesus,' gospel-clarity in their public descriptions. Pastor John Butler appears to be a Word-focused leader. The 318 Emancipation Hwy location puts them in a community-facing context. Key concerns: Pastor Melanie's co-pastor role raises complementarian questions, the independent structure has no external accountability, and the Pentecostal/charismatic culture may lean experiential. LWC3 appears to be a sincere, Christ-centered ministry serving their community — not red-flagged theologically on the essentials, but the co-pastor structure and independence are watch items for a man who values clear authority and accountability.

churches.name: Selah Church
churches.assessment: Selah is a young, Spirit-filled church led by genuinely gospel-loving people. Luke Taylor is a sincere pastor with solid theology on the essentials — Christ is the only way, the Bible is authoritative, gender is binary. But structural concerns are real: no elder accountability, women functioning in pastoral roles, and a spiritual formation emphasis that can trend contemplative rather than expository. If you're a man who needs clear authority structures and complementarian conviction, visit with your eyes open. If you're a new believer or seeking family, you'll find genuine love here. Just ask the hard questions early.

churches.assessment: Revive Church is a vibrant, mission-focused charismatic church with clear evangelical convictions on salvation and the centrality of Christ. The 'house for God's presence' framing reflects a genuine Spirit-first culture. Key watch items: Jeremy and Erica Duggins serve as co-lead pastors (Erica's pastoral title is a complementarian yellow flag), no visible elder accountability structure, and the presence/experience emphasis may crowd out systematic biblical teaching. Friend Aaron Ranford attends — worth a personal conversation about what he's found there doctrinally. Could be a great community for mission-minded men who are strong in their own theology.

churches.name: St. George's Episcopal Church
churches.pastor: The Rev. Joseph H. Hensley Jr.
churches.pastor_credentials: DMin, Virginia Theological Seminary; ordained deacon and priest 2007; rector since 2015
churches.services: Multiple Sunday services (call office for times: 540-373-4133)

score_notes.christology: Nominally affirms Christ but TEC's broad inclusivism increasingly softens exclusivity claims
score_notes.scripture: The Episcopal Church (TEC) has formally departed from biblical authority on sexuality and gender — affirms same-sex marriage, LGBTQ+ ordination
score_notes.gender: Explicitly advertises inclusivity of 'sexual orientation and gender expression'; women are ordained priests and bishops in TEC; he/him pronouns listed voluntarily in staff bios
score_notes.leadership: Women serve in all clergy roles including rector; no male-elder requirement; diocesan leadership is progressive
score_notes.soteriology: Episcopal tradition broadly views salvation; TEC leans universalist in practice if not confession
score_notes.cultural: Facebook page explicitly states 'You are welcome here inclusive of race, nationality, sexual orientation, gender expression' — DEI language built into church identity
score_notes.denomination: Diocese of Virginia provides accountability but to progressive denominational hierarchy
score_notes.preaching: Liturgical/lectionary-based; homilies typically brief and thematic rather than expository
score_notes.mens: No evidence of intentional men's discipleship; primary community focus
score_notes.mission: Service and community orientation; Great Commission clarity unclear

churches.assessment: St. George's is a historic colonial-era church with a beautiful building and rich liturgical tradition, but The Episcopal Church has made formal institutional commitments to LGBTQ+ affirmation that place it outside biblical alignment on sexuality, gender, and in many ways Scripture's final authority. The rector is credentialed and experienced, but VTS (Virginia Theological Seminary) is among the most progressive Episcopal seminaries. For Moop who applied for employment here — the job opportunity doesn't require theological agreement, but discipleship-wise this is not the church to call home.

score_notes.leadership: No leadership team info found publicly; small community church with limited web presence
score_notes.denomination: Independent; no denominational accountability structure visible
score_notes.preaching: Preaching style unknown; small church with limited online content to evaluate

churches.assessment: Fawn Lake Church has an encouraging doctrinal foundation — they explicitly affirm Trinitarian orthodoxy, biblical inspiration, and salvation through Christ alone. Their mission statement includes both Great Commission language and community reconciliation, which is healthy. The church is small and community-focused, meeting at Laurel Hill Chapel. Major unknowns: who leads it, what preaching style looks like, stance on gender roles, and whether there's any substantive discipleship infrastructure. Moop applied here for employment — before any deeper relationship, worth attending a service and asking direct questions about leadership, accountability, and biblical authority on gender/sexuality.

churches.name: The Mount Church (Fredericksburg Campus)
churches.pastor_credentials: B.A. in Missions, Trinity Baptist College (Jacksonville, FL); former missionary in Poland (2.5 years)
churches.founded: Unknown (formerly Mount Ararat Church; rebranded as The Mount)
churches.denomination: Baptist (affiliated with BGAV — Baptist General Association of Virginia)
churches.services: Sunday mornings (live worship; teaching streamed from Stafford campus)

score_notes.gender: BGAV (Baptist General Association of Virginia) is the moderate/progressive Virginia Baptist body — allows women in pastoral roles; stance unclear at local campus level
score_notes.leadership: Campus pastor model; primary teaching comes via video/stream from Stafford campus rather than local preacher — reduces direct pastoral relationship
score_notes.cultural: BGAV affiliation carries moderate Baptist drift risk; no explicit DEI language found but denomination leans progressive compared to SBC
score_notes.denomination: BGAV affiliation (not SBC); BGAV is the 'Cooperative Baptist Fellowship'-adjacent body in Virginia — moderate theologically
score_notes.preaching: Multi-site model: Fredericksburg campus receives sermon via video from Stafford; Andrew Brothers leads local worship but doesn't preach weekly
score_notes.mens: No dedicated men's discipleship program found for Fredericksburg campus

churches.assessment: The Mount Fredericksburg has a campus pastor, Andrew Brothers, with a solid missions background and genuine evangelistic heart. The 'church For One More' vision is outreach-forward in a healthy way, and the Baptist DNA keeps the basics in place. Two key concerns: (1) BGAV affiliation places them in the moderate Virginia Baptist stream rather than SBC — BGAV allows women pastors and leans progressive denominationally; (2) the multi-site streaming model means the congregation watches Stafford's sermon via video rather than hearing Andrew preach, which weakens local pastoral voice and relationship. Worth a visit; go in knowing you're in moderate Baptist territory, not SBC.

churches.name: Spotswood Baptist Church
churches.pastor: Dr. Drew Landry (Senior Pastor); Dr. Dan Cook (Executive Pastor / Minister of Education, serving since 1994)
churches.pastor_credentials: Dan Cook: BS Pastoral Theology (Hyles-Anderson College), MA Religion + MA Religious Education (Liberty Baptist Theological Seminary), EdD (Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary)
churches.founded: Pre-1994 (established; Dr. Cook has served since 1994)
churches.denomination: Southern Baptist Convention (SBC of Virginia / SBCV)

score_notes.mens: Dr. Cook oversees all discipleship and adult ministries with passion for small-group disciple-making, but no standalone men's ministry specifically confirmed on website

churches.assessment: Spotswood Baptist is the most theologically squared-up church on this list. SBC affiliation means clear complementarian conviction, Scripture inerrancy, and Great Commission focus. Dr. Drew Landry leads as senior pastor while Dr. Dan Cook — who has served since 1994 with degrees from Liberty and Southeastern Baptist — provides deep discipleship infrastructure. The values (Vertical Worship, Transformational Teaching, Biblical Community, Missional Living) map cleanly onto what a man seeking solid formation needs. Two services on Sundays, well-resourced, clearly evangelical. Moop has a meeting with Dr. Cook — that relationship alone is worth pursuing. This is a church worth taking seriously.
